claim: H14/H89/L93 do not contact the steroid
finding: min heavy-atom distance 9.33 A (res14, n=2), 12.86-15.38 A (res89, n=7), 13.22-13.60 A (res93, n=7); first-shell residues 2.59-3.95 A
context: human CBG crystal structures, cleaved R state, cortisol/progesterone
confidence: high; res14 modelled in only 2 of 8 chains

claim: the three positions form one contacting cluster
confidence: high for 89-93; 14 pairs from 2 chains only

claim: the cluster is "centred on helix D"
finding: helix D = CBG 79-96 (4th helix, as in a1-antitrypsin 1QLP 88-104); H89 and L93 are inside it, H14 is in the pre-helix-A segment and only contacts it (3.87-4.30 A)
context: serpin helix nomenclature by sequence order

claim: the helix D connecting loop moves with ligand occupancy
finding: published ">8 A" shift reproduced as 8.85 A at residue 100; all other elements <1.2 A mean in the same-species comparison
context: human cleaved CBG, apo vs cortisol, identical numbering

claim: helix D itself moves between native and cleaved states
finding: helix D 1.80 A mean vs steroid wall 0.65 A, but helices C/E/F differ 2.78-2.83 A from species alone; helix D sits inside that noise band
context: rat native (2V95) vs human cleaved (2VDY), 61.0% mature identity
confidence: moderate; no native human CBG structure exists, so this is cross-species

claim: the requested native-vs-cleaved analysis can be run in human
finding: all five human entries (2VDX,2VDY,4BB2,4C41,4C49) are reactive-loop-cleaved; 2V95 (rat) is the only native structure

claim: the cluster couples to the site through the helix D connecting loop
finding: shortest paths reach a steroid contact in 2-3 hops via the N-terminal segment and F369/T370 (H14-R15-A18; L93-T370-A18; H89-G86-L17-A18) but reach the mobile 97-101 loop only in 3-4 hops
context: 4.5 A residue contact graph, 363 nodes, 1778 edges
confidence: moderate; unweighted path length is a coarse proxy for allosteric coupling

claim: the cluster residues participate in the ligand-coupled motion
finding: H89 shifts 0.54 A and L93 0.99 A, while the hinge begins at A95 (3.36 A) and peaks at residue 100 (8.85 A); L93 is the last static residue and contacts S97 at 3.50 A
context: human cleaved CBG, apo vs cortisol

claim: His89 is a conserved allosteric hotspot
finding: H89 conserved in only 60% of orthologues; Tyr (the human H89Y substitution) is wild type in rat, mouse, rabbit, beaver and wombat. L93 90%, H14 84%, comparable to W371 90%
confidence: high; pairwise alignment, rat anchored by invariant L90/L93

claim: all four substitutions lower cortisol-binding affinity
finding: H14Q and H89Y markedly reduce affinity, but H14R reduces binding capacity; R260L abolishes binding
context: human CBG mutants expressed in CHO cells, cortisol-binding activity and ELISA
confidence: high for the readouts; no Kd values reported in the abstract

finding: Kd 2.24 +/- 1.75 nM vs 0.64 +/- 0.31 nM wild type, p<0.024 (3.5-fold); same-patient S224A control unaffected (0.63 +/- 0.33 nM)
context: CHO-expressed human CBG, Scatchard analysis, single patient kindred
confidence: low-moderate; wide SD, borderline p, single study, never replicated

claim: these variants are a coherent set of deficiency alleles
finding: AF spans 3600-fold: L93H 2.49e-3 with 2 homozygotes (2nd most common of 534 missense), H14R 1.62e-4, H89Y 2.33e-5, H14Q 6.84e-7; SERPINA6 missense o/e 0.938, mis_z 0.59, pLI 1.9e-5
context: gnomAD v4 exomes, AN approx 1.46 million

claim: the variant and binding-site annotation is complete
finding: only 3 natural variants annotated (L93H, S224A, D367N); H14Q/H14R/H89Y absent. Only 4 of the 13 residues within 4.5 A of cortisol are annotated as binding sites; F369 and T370 are not
